note: The per-role quantization policy (I4). It is data: changing what is quantized is changing this file, not the code. A role that is absent from 'quant' stops the install rather than defaulting. `router.logits` is bf16 because I3 says the discrete decisions must survive; the shared expert is bf16 because it is active on every token, unlike a routed expert.

why.norms, embedding and head: I3: gating and normalisation decide the discrete outcomes; they stay at bf16 or above. The head is tied to the embedding, so quantizing it would quantize the embedding twice over.
why.attn.q_norm / attn.k_norm / linear.norm: per-head normalisation vectors, one per head dimension: quantizing 256 numbers to 4 bits saves nothing measurable and costs accuracy
why.linear.a_log / linear.dt_bias: the Gated DeltaNet's decay is exponentiated; a 4-bit error there is not a small error
why.linear.in_a / linear.in_b / linear.conv: the gates and the causal convolution: small, and on the path that decides how much state to keep
why.router.logits: I3, and the brief says it in as many words: quantizing the router flips marginal argmax results, and the output then diverges completely while every per-tensor check still looks green. Sixteen thousand numbers per layer is not where the bytes are.
why.expert.stack_gate_up / expert.stack_down: The routed experts: 92.9% of this model's parameters, and the only reason M1 exists. This is where 4-bit earns its error budget.
why.expert.shared.*: The shared expert is on EVERY token, unlike a routed expert which serves eight tokens in 256. Its error is not amortised, and it is 3% of the parameters: quantizing it would spend accuracy on the dense path to save nothing measurable.
why.expert.shared.scalar: One row of 2048 numbers that scales a whole branch of the mixture. It costs nothing to keep at fp32 and a 4-bit error there multiplies everything the shared expert produces.
